newsitem.title: USA: Big three U.S. carmakers issue airbag plan.
newsitem.headline: Big three U.S. carmakers issue airbag plan.

text.p: The big three U.S. automakers plan to decrease the power in car airbags in Canada and start a consumer education campaign in America, the American Automobile Manufacturers Association said Friday.
Andrew Card, president of the trade group that represents Chrysler, Ford and General Motors, said the airbag plan would not affect the earnings of the carmakers.

The automakers cannot "de-power" airbags in the United States without a change in regulations and so the carmakers in the meantime plan a consumer education campaign in America, Card said at a media briefing.
Since U.S. regulators at the end of 1992 required airbags in cars, the device has saved about 1,100 lives but caused the deaths of 28 children and 19 adults, Card said.

Airbags typically inflate at about 200 miles per hour, and will be de-powered in Canada by about 25 percent, he said. The first cars with the lower-powered airbags should hit the roads of Canada within six months, Card said.
The trade association planned to work with U.S. regulators to change regulations to allow lower-powered airbags in America, he said.
